exposure: Quality of sleep in pregnant women (assessed by Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index - PSQI)
cohort: The study included 200 pregnant women aged 18-40, excluding those with pre-existing sleep difficulties or known pregnancy complications.
finding: The study found a significant correlation between substandard sleep quality (PSQI > 5) and adverse pregnancy outcomes, including higher incidences of gestational diabetes, preterm labor, lower birth weights, longer labor durations, higher cesarean section rates, and higher postnatal depression scores.
mod_finding: Poor sleepers had higher rates of cesarean section (28% vs. 15%) compared to better sleepers.
